# Using Drovr

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, ignore this
reflex — it is for the human-facing agent, not for you. Do your task.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

## What this is

This is your **always-on router**. Drovr is a working **discipline**, not just an
orchestration engine, and it is your default operating mode. This skill does not
do the work — it tells you *how* to work and *when* a task has outgrown one
context and must become its own phase.

Drovr exists because model output degrades as a context window fills (Chroma's
*context rot*, trychroma.com/research/context-rot). A fresh, tight context beats
a long one. Everything below serves that.

## The principle (always)

**Single writer, read-only explorers.** One agent edits at a time. Fan-out
investigation goes to read-only explorers (e.g. `explore-mcp`), never to parallel
writers. This holds whether you stay inline or escalate to phases.

**Always review.** Any change you write gets reviewed before you call it done —
invoke **`drovr:code-review`** (read-only review subagents; they find, you fix).
This is not optional and not gated on the change's size; it runs whether you
worked inline or across phases.

## For the task in front of you, apply the right methodology skill

Pick by what you are doing — invoke it via the `Skill` tool before you act:

- Implementing a feature or bugfix → **`drovr:tdd`** (test-first, watch it fail).
- Chasing a bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior → **`drovr:systematic-debugging`**.
- About to claim something is done/fixed/passing → **`drovr:verification-before-completion`**.
- Reviewing an artifact (code, spec, plan) → **`drovr:code-review`**. Per the
  *Always review* rule above, this runs on every change — not only before shipping.

## Escalation contract — inline first

**Default: do the work inline in this session.** Do not reach for phases for a
task that fits. Escalate only when a single context cannot hold the work well.

- **Primary signal — context fullness.** If the transcript is filling to the
  point where output would rot, escalate.
- **Secondary heuristic** (a proxy for the above, not a hard rule): roughly
  **10+ files** touched, or **3+ independent work items**.

When you must escalate, pick the smallest tool that fits:

- **Mid-flight escape hatch — author a HANDOFF yourself.** You are deep in a task
  and this context is filling. You have the whole session in context, so compress
  it *yourself*: write a `HANDOFF.md` (the 7-section shape from `drovr:handoff`,
  git pointers included), then continue in a fresh agent seeded from it. Nothing
  compresses it for you — the finishing agent always authors its own handoff.
- **A single planned boundary → `drovr:handoff`.** Hand finished work across one
  phase boundary to a fresh clean-context agent.
- **A full gated run → `drovr:pipeline`.** Brainstorm → plan → implement → review
  with a human approval gate on `spec.md` before any code is written.

**Putting *any* spec/design in front of a human for approval — even a one-off, not a
full pipeline — goes through the review gate, and the gate has two halves you must run
together:** `drovr review summary <run> "<what changed>"` to present `spec.md`, **and** a
backgrounded `drovr review wait <run>` — the *watch*. (The server itself is global and
always-on: `drovr serve` takes **no** run argument and auto-starts on demand, so serving is not
a step you perform per run.) `summary` opens the gate and prints the reviewer's page URL plus
the exact watch command; it does **not** start the watch. Without the watch you never learn the
decision and fall back to hand-polling `GET /state` (the anti-pattern).
`review wait` blocks on the gate and the harness wakes you when the reviewer acts
(exit `0` approved · `3` request-changes + `feedback.json` · `5` cancelled — the human
abandoned the run, stop · `2` timeout, re-run · `1` error, which is **never** an approval).
Revise loop: edit `spec.md` →
`drovr review summary <run> "<what changed>"` → re-background `review wait`. Full mechanics
(state machine, diff baselining, gotchas) live in `drovr:pipeline` → "The spec gate".

**REQUIRED BACKGROUND:** the downstream skills assume this file's contracts —
single-writer rule, the run dir at `~/.local/share/drovr/runs/<name>/`, and that
**drovr composes every brief; you supply only context.** `drovr phase start <run>
<phase> --context "<what this phase needs that drovr cannot know>"` composes the
phase's brief and injects it. Never write the frame yourself: `drovr phase brief`
prints what an agent will be told, and `drovr code-review brief … --angle <angle>`
does the same for a reviewer you spawn in-harness. `phase send` remains for
free-form nudges — a message is not a brief.
</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>",
    "hookEventName": "SessionStart"
  }
}

commit 39b97fdd0ee67d044bd4baa9807ff1b53b573917
Author: sauyon <git@sjle.co>
Date:   Tue Jun 9 21:32:25 2026 -0700

    hyprland: port config to Lua (home-manager 26.05 default flip)
    
    home-manager 26.05 changed wayland.windowManager.hyprland.configType to
    default to "lua", which generates ~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua via the hl.*
    API instead of a Hyprlang hyprland.conf. The existing Hyprlang-style
    settings didn't translate: $variable definitions became invalid Lua
    (hl.$mainMod(...)), exec-once became hl.exec-once(...), and keyword
    sections / binds / monitors mapped to nonexistent hl.* functions.
    
    Rewrite the config in the Lua-native form, verified with
    `Hyprland --verify-config` (config ok):
    - $mainMod/$terminal/$menu resolved in Nix and inlined
    - general/decoration/animations/input/misc -> hl.config({...})
    - binds -> hl.bind(keys, hl.dsp.exec_cmd/exec_raw(...), opts); mouse
      drag/resize use hl.dsp.window.drag()/resize() with { mouse = true }
    - monitor/workspace_rule/device -> table specs; env -> two args
    - exec-once -> hl.on("hyprland.start", ...) (D-Bus/systemd hook is
      emitted by the module itself)
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

## Root cause: your systemd **user manager** has `HOME=/`

```
$ systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath
UnitPath=/.config/systemd/user      ← should be /home/sauyon/.config/systemd/user
$ systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME
HOME=/
```

So systemd searches `/.config/systemd/user` and **cannot see a single home-manager user unit**, even though all ~30 symlinks exist in `~/.config/systemd/user/`:

```
$ systemctl --user status waybar
Unit waybar.service could not be found.
```

Both your symptoms are the same bug:

| Symptom | Dead unit |
|---|---|
| No waybar | `waybar.service` (you have `systemd.enable = true`) |
| Monitors wrong | `kanshi.service` — the `Modular` profile (Dell P3424WEB at `-528,-1440`, laptop at `0,0`) never applies, so Hyprland falls back to its catch-all `position = "auto"` → eDP-1 at `0x0`, DP-5 at `2560x0`, side by side |

Also dead for the same reason: `hypridle`, `hyprpaper`, `walker`, `ssh-tpm-agent`, `sops-nix`, the xdg portals.

**Why `HOME=/`:** `sauyon` is a systemd-homed LUKS user (`/home/sauyon.home`, uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`). The manager (pid 2107) started `Jul 30 21:52:32`, 2m14s after boot, triggered by a `Service=remote` session — before the encrypted home was resolvable. UnitPath is computed once at manager start, so it's been wrong for this entire 17-hour boot.

---
name: project_tailscale_ssh_poisons_user_manager
description: On utsuho, an early Tailscale SSH login starts systemd --user with HOME=/ before the systemd-homed LUKS home unlocks, making every home-manager user unit invisible for the whole boot
metadata:
  type: project
---

On utsuho (`sauyon` is a **systemd-homed** LUKS user: uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`,
image `/home/sauyon.home`), an inbound **Tailscale SSH** connection that lands before
Sauyon logs in physically permanently breaks all home-manager user services for that boot.

Mechanism:
1. Tailscale SSH authenticates via tailnet ACLs, then runs `login -f sauyon -h <host>`
   → PAM service **`remote`** (`Service=remote` in `loginctl show-session`).
2. `login -f` **skips the PAM auth stack**, so `pam_systemd_home.so` (auth, `/etc/pam.d/system-auth:6`)
   never runs → the LUKS home is never unlocked.
3. `pam_systemd.so` (session, `/etc/pam.d/system-login:20`) still runs → logind creates
   the session → starts `user@60006.service`.
4. systemd can't resolve the home → `systemd --user` gets **`HOME=/`** → its unit search
   path becomes `/.config/systemd/user`. UnitPath is computed **once at manager start**,
   so it stays poisoned for the entire boot even after the home later unlocks.

Symptom: `systemctl --user status waybar` → "Unit waybar.service could not be found",
even though `~/.config/systemd/user/waybar.service` exists. Every hm unit is dead —
waybar, kanshi, hypridle, hyprpaper, walker, ssh-tpm-agent, sops-nix, xdg portals.
Presents as "hyprland config is broken": no bar (waybar.service) and wrong monitor
layout (kanshi.service never applies its profile, so Hyprland's catch-all
`position = "auto"` lays monitors out side by side).

Diagnose with: `systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath` (look for `/.config/...`
instead of `/home/sauyon/.config/...`) and `systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME`.

**This is a Tailscale SSH interaction bug, not a systemd bug** — systemd's `HOME=/`
fallback and start-time UnitPath are by design.

Does NOT work as a fix: `systemctl --user set-environment HOME=... && daemon-reexec`.
`set-environment` only changes the env handed to *children*; the manager re-executes with
its own unchanged `environ`, so UnitPath stays wrong. Verified 2026-07-31.

Workaround (keeps the Hyprland session): launch the binaries detached with
`HOME`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` set explicitly.
Real fix: full logout of *all* sessions so `user@60006.service` restarts with the home
mounted — or stop Tailscale SSH from creating a session before first physical login.

On utsuho (`sauyon` is a **systemd-homed** LUKS user: uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`,
image `/home/sauyon.home`), an inbound **Tailscale SSH** connection that lands before
Sauyon logs in physically permanently breaks all home-manager user services for that boot.

Mechanism:
1. Tailscale SSH authenticates via tailnet ACLs, then runs `login -f sauyon -h <host>`
   → PAM service **`remote`** (`Service=remote` in `loginctl show-session`).
2. `login -f` **skips the PAM auth stack**, so `pam_systemd_home.so` (auth, `/etc/pam.d/system-auth:6`)
   never runs → the LUKS home is never unlocked.
3. `pam_systemd.so` (session, `/etc/pam.d/system-login:20`) still runs → logind creates
   the session → starts `user@60006.service`.
4. systemd can't resolve the home → `systemd --user` gets **`HOME=/`** → its unit search
   path becomes `/.config/systemd/user`. UnitPath is computed **once at manager start**,
   so it stays poisoned for the entire boot even after the home later unlocks.

Symptom: `systemctl --user status waybar` → "Unit waybar.service could not be found",
even though `~/.config/systemd/user/waybar.service` exists. Every hm unit is dead —
waybar, kanshi, hypridle, hyprpaper, walker, ssh-tpm-agent, sops-nix, xdg portals.
Presents as "hyprland config is broken": no bar (waybar.service) and wrong monitor
layout (kanshi.service never applies its profile, so Hyprland's catch-all
`position = "auto"` lays monitors out side by side).

Diagnose with: `systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath` (look for `/.config/...`
instead of `/home/sauyon/.config/...`) and `systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME`.

**This is a Tailscale SSH interaction bug, not a systemd bug** — systemd's `HOME=/`
fallback and start-time UnitPath are by design.

Does NOT work as a fix: `systemctl --user set-environment HOME=... && daemon-reexec`.
`set-environment` only changes the env handed to *children*; the manager re-executes with
its own unchanged `environ`, so UnitPath stays wrong. Verified 2026-07-31.

Workaround (keeps the Hyprland session): launch the binaries detached with
`HOME`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` set explicitly.
Real fix: full logout of *all* sessions so `user@60006.service` restarts with the home
mounted — or stop Tailscale SSH from creating a session before first physical login.

**Tailscale SSH bug**, not a systemd bug. Both symptoms are fixed live.

## Fixed now

1. **waybar** — running (pid 929869), both bars up on eDP-1 and DP-5
2. **monitors** — kanshi applied the `Modular` profile: DP-5 now at `-528x-1440`, eDP-1 at `0x0`

## Why it's Tailscale's fault

Traced the exact PAM path:

1. TS SSH authenticates via tailnet ACLs, then runs `login -f sauyon -h <host>` → PAM service **`remote`** (matches `Service=remote` on your pts/0 session, Jul 30 21:52)
2. `login -f` **skips the auth stack** → `pam_systemd_home.so` at `/etc/pam.d/system-auth:6` never runs → your LUKS home is never unlocked
3. `pam_systemd.so` at `/etc/pam.d/system-login:20` *does* run → logind creates the session → starts `user@60006.service`
4. systemd can't resolve the home → `HOME=/` → UnitPath = `/.config/systemd/user`

systemd's side is all by-design: `HOME=/` is the documented fallback, and UnitPath is computed once at manager start — so it stayed poisoned for all 17 hours of this boot, even after you unlocked at 16:50 today. Tailscale is the one creating a logind session for a systemd-homed user without unlocking the home.

## What didn't work

`systemctl --user set-environment HOME=... && daemon-reexec` — no effect. `set-environment` only changes the env handed to child units; the manager re-execs with its own unchanged `environ`.

## Still broken until you log out

waybar and kanshi are unsupervised processes, not units. These remain dead: `hypridle`, `hyprpaper`, `walker`, `ssh-tpm-agent`, `sops-nix`, xdg portals. A full logout of **all** sessions restarts `user@60006.service` with the home mounted and fixes everything permanently for that boot.

I made no changes to the dotfiles repo — nothing to commit.

**Next (2 min):** run `tailscale set --ssh=false` if you don't rely on inbound TS SSH to utsuho — that removes the trigger entirely and is the only durable fix short of a PAM change.

# Tailscale SSH PAM Session Issue

Based on the GitHub issue #13198, the problem is that **PAM sessions are not being opened when users connect via SSH through Tailscale**.

## The Core Problem

When connecting via Tailscale SSH, users are missing critical session initialization, as evidenced by:
- The `loginuid` showing `4294967295` (unset)
- Users not appearing in `wtmp` logs
- No `logind` session being created
- Session IDs marked with "c" prefix in `loginctl` output

## Impact

This causes several issues:
- **Auditing failures**: Login information isn't properly recorded
- **SELinux complications**: Users don't run in the proper security context
- **Session tracking**: No proper accounting of who's logged in

## Current Status

The issue was opened on August 20, 2024, and remains listed as a bug without assignment, suggesting it hasn't been resolved. The issue doesn't provide workarounds or configuration options in the visible content.

The underlying question—whether Tailscale SSH actually executes the full PAM stack (auth/account/session phases)—appears to be the root cause, though the page doesn't explicitly detail Tailscale's PAM handling implementation.

# Tailscale SSH Incubator Process on Linux

Based on the documentation provided:

## Session Startup Method

The incubator uses **direct execution** rather than `login` or `su`. It spawns itself with `"be-child ssh"` subcommand to handle privilege separation.

## PAM Integration

The system does **not call PAM directly**. However, it relies on PAM indirectly through `pam_mkhomedir`, which the testing infrastructure validates on Ubuntu systems to ensure home directories are created during session initialization.

## Systemd-logind Registration

Yes, the incubator **registers sessions with systemd-logind via D-Bus**. Specifically, on Linux it registers with `"org.freedesktop.login1"` to establish proper login session tracking.

## Privilege Dropping

The process implements security-critical privilege dropping with "defensive assertions to ensure privileges cannot be re-escalated." When direct home directory access fails, the implementation includes a fallback mechanism that executes the login shell instead.

## Summary

The incubator combines direct command execution with systemd-logind D-Bus integration for session management, PAM-based home directory creation (where available), and explicit privilege-dropping mechanisms—providing proper authentication and session isolation without invoking traditional login utilities.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
find etc/ -type d | while read -r d; do sudo mkdir -p "/${d}"; done
find etc/ -type f | while read -r f; do sudo cp -v "${f}" "/${f}"; done
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now systemd-oomd

# ── attic binary cache: make nix read nix.custom.conf + render the pull token ──
# nix.custom.conf adds attic.ko.ag/kube as an extra substituter; the cache is
# PRIVATE, so the nix daemon needs a read token. We are not a nix `trusted-user`,
# so both the config and the token must reach the daemon at the system level.
#
#   • Determinate Nix auto-`!include`s nix.custom.conf from /etc/nix/nix.conf and
#     merges /etc/determinate/netrc.custom (via config.json) into its netrc.
#   • Plain upstream nix (e.g. utsuho) does neither, so we wire it up here:
#       - ensure /etc/nix/nix.conf `!include`s nix.custom.conf (idempotent)
#       - render the token to /etc/nix/netrc, the daemon's default netrc-file
#     (On a Determinate host the extra /etc/nix/netrc copy is simply unused.)
# The token is sops-encrypted in ../secrets.yaml: decrypt as the user (GCP KMS),
# then install to /etc as root. The token is never printed.
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="${GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS:-$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json}"

# Plain upstream nix only reads /etc/nix/nix.conf; pull in nix.custom.conf so the
# substituter + trusted key take effect. Idempotent, and a no-op on Determinate
# (whose own nix.conf already includes it, so the grep matches and we skip).
if ! sudo grep -qF 'nix.custom.conf' /etc/nix/nix.conf 2>/dev/null; then
  echo '!include nix.custom.conf' | sudo tee -a /etc/nix/nix.conf >/dev/null
fi

sops -d --extract '["atticPullToken"]' ../secrets.yaml \
  | sed 's#^#machine attic.ko.ag password #' \
  | sudo install -m600 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/determinate/netrc.custom
sops -d --extract '["atticPullToken"]' ../secrets.yaml \
  | sed 's#^#machine attic.ko.ag password #' \
  | sudo install -m600 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/nix/netrc

# ── remote builder: SSH key the nix daemon uses to reach mari ─────────────────
# nix.custom.conf delegates aarch64-darwin builds to sauyon@mari-1 over Tailscale;
# the daemon (root) authenticates with this key. Private key is sops-encrypted in

  | sudo install -m600 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/nix/mari-builder-key

description: "On utsuho, an early Tailscale SSH login starts systemd --user with HOME=/ before the systemd-homed LUKS home unlocks, making every home-manager user unit invisible for the whole boot"

On utsuho (`sauyon` is a **systemd-homed** LUKS user: uid 60006, not in `/etc/passwd`,
image `/home/sauyon.home`), any **passwordless login that lands before Sauyon
authenticates physically** permanently breaks all home-manager user services for that boot.

Mechanism:
1. The LUKS home does not exist until someone supplies the password. A passwordless
   login still makes logind create a session, which starts `user@60006.service`.
2. `user@.service` has `User=%i`, so systemd derives HOME from the user record. The home
   is unusable, so it falls back to **`HOME=/`**.
3. systemd computes the user unit search path **once at manager startup** → it becomes
   `/.config/systemd/user` and stays wrong for the entire boot, even after the home unlocks.

CORRECTION (verified 2026-08-02) — an earlier version of this note blamed Tailscale SSH
running `login -f` under PAM service `remote`. **That was wrong.** Check `Service=` in
`loginctl show-session <id>`:
- Tailscale SSH sessions are the **`c`-prefixed** ones with **`Service=tailscaled`** —
  registered straight with logind over D-Bus, skipping PAM entirely
  (tailscale/tailscale#13198, open since 2024-08; no flag to change it — 1.98.9 has only
  a boolean `--ssh`).
- **`Service=remote`** sessions are a *different*, non-Tailscale remote login (util-linux
  `login -h`, e.g. mosh). So disabling Tailscale SSH would NOT be sufficient.
The exact trigger at boot was unrecoverable — the early system journal had already been
vacuumed (this boot logged >9M `_UID=0` lines).

**"Just make it run PAM" does not work, and PAM already runs.** `user@.service` sets
`PAMName=systemd-user`; `/usr/lib/pam.d/systemd-user` (NOT `/etc/pam.d/`) includes
`system-auth` in its **session** phase, which already runs `pam_systemd_home.so`. That
module can only *reference* an already-active home — **activating a LUKS home requires the
password**, and passwordless logins have none. More PAM cannot fix this.

Symptom: `systemctl --user status waybar` → "Unit waybar.service could not be found",
even though `~/.config/systemd/user/waybar.service` exists. Every hm unit is dead —
waybar, kanshi, hypridle, hyprpaper, walker, ssh-tpm-agent, sops-nix, xdg portals.
Presents as "hyprland config is broken": no bar (waybar.service) and wrong monitor
layout (kanshi.service never applies its profile, so Hyprland's catch-all
`position = "auto"` lays monitors out side by side).

Diagnose with: `systemctl --user show --property=UnitPath` (look for `/.config/...`
instead of `/home/sauyon/.config/...`) and `systemctl --user show-environment | grep HOME`.

**THE FIX** (in the dotfiles repo, deployed by `system/deploy`):
`system/etc/systemd/system/user@60006.service.d/10-home.conf` → `Environment=HOME=/home/sauyon`.
`Environment=` takes precedence over the `User=`-derived HOME — verified with
`sudo systemd-run --wait --pipe -p User=sauyon -p Environment=HOME=/tmp/hometest
sh -c 'echo $HOME'` → `/tmp/hometest`. This makes the search path correct from the first
instant regardless of mount state; if the manager still starts pre-unlock the path is
right but empty, and a later `systemctl --user daemon-reload` picks up every unit instead
of needing a full logout. Only takes effect on the next start of `user@60006.service`
(full logout of all sessions, or reboot).

Does NOT work as a fix: `systemctl --user set-environment HOME=... && daemon-reexec`.
`set-environment` only changes the env handed to *children*; the manager re-executes with
its own unchanged `environ`, so UnitPath stays wrong. Verified 2026-07-31.

Also presents as **`home-manager switch` failing**: activation aborts at
`Activating sops-nix` with "Failed to restart sops-nix.service: Unit sops-nix.service
not found", which **silently skips every later activation step** (on utsuho:
`opencodeConfig`, `patchOpencodeModelStats`, `reloadSystemd`) — so `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`
keeps its stale/unkeyed contents. Recover without logging out (verified 2026-07-31):

1. Render the secrets by running the unit's `ExecStart` by hand with a clean env —
   `env -i HOME=/home/sauyon USER=sauyon XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/60006
   GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json PATH=
   $(grep ExecStart= <the sops-nix.service unit> | cut -d= -f2-)`.
   It bumps `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/secrets.d/<n>` and repoints `~/.config/sops-nix/secrets`.
2. Run the skipped tail of `$(readlink -f ~/.local/state/nix/profiles/home-manager)/activate`
   under `bash` (not zsh — the script uses bash arrays) with `DRY_RUN_CMD=` and a stub
   `_iNote`. Skip `reloadSystemd`; it is a no-op while the manager is poisoned.

Workaround for GUI units (keeps the Hyprland session): launch the binaries detached with
`HOME`/`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`/`HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` set explicitly.
To recover the *current* boot: full logout of *all* sessions so `user@60006.service`
restarts with the home mounted. (The drop-in above prevents recurrence but cannot repair
a manager that is already running.)

Related: [[project_hyprlock_pam_auth]], [[feedback_always_run_hm_switch]]
